name: Magpiash
overview: Magpiash is a male biblical figure identified as a non-Levite leader mentioned in Nehemiah 10:14. He is noted specifically for his inclusion on the sealed covenant document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27, highlighting his role among the leaders who pledged commitment during the post-exilic period. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, his leadership position is distinctive due to being outside the Levitical priestly class.
namesAndTitles: The name Magpiash means 'moth killer,' a proper name recorded in Nehemiah 10:20. This name is not indicated as being given directly by God but reflects a meaningful Hebrew term associated with him.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Magpiash as a descendant of Jacob, establishing his Israelite heritage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded, and no tribal affiliation is given apart from his non-Levite status.
scriptureSignificance: Magpiash's significance lies in his role as a non-Levite leader who was part of the covenant community committing to uphold God's law after the return from exile. His inclusion on the sealed document in Nehemiah 10:20 underscores his recognized leadership and dedication to the communal restoration efforts under God's guidance. This highlights the broader participation of Israelite leaders beyond the priestly tribe in the renewal of covenant faithfulness.
